observations: Printed p.177 Figs.2–3 and the adjacent table label the final graffito1 sign w(?) / N6; p.178 makes that preference conditional on discounting a stroke. Fig.1 is a published object photograph; the project has not examined the object.

Printed p.178 n.11 distinguishes N22 sign identity from a/a2/V notation. Printed p.182 n.20 reports the historical N6/N7 value reversal, still not conclusive. Rizza–Zinko’s p.144 table separately retains N22 as V (Vokal). Shared name evidence does not identify Abydos graffiti with S9.

The supplied Sidetic in Egypt p.191–192 prints Pojau for Abydos graffito1 and argues that its final letter is the new u-like sign, formerly confused with N02 e variants. Its p.192 photographs are credited to Susana Soler and dated4 December2022. This is an attributed alternative to Phillips–Rutherford’s qualified final w(?), not a settled project reading.

At pp.192–193 Ferrer–Soler–Adiego also allow one letter written over the other, with the order unknown. At pp.190–191 they describe initially independent submissions but acknowledge consulting Phillips–Rutherford’s original article; the published revision focuses exclusively on graffito1. Two papers and two photographs do not create additional ancient witnesses or independent expert reviews.
remaining_work: The selected two-edition documentary comparison is complete; the final u versus w(?) or possible overwritten-sign question remains unadjudicated. Preserve each author’s letter labels and j/y conventions; the full new-vowel argument in Ferrer’s separate Kadmos article was not rechecked by this receipt.

Keep N22/S9.6 vowel disagreement separate from the proposed split of N02 e variants. Brixhe–Neumann1988, current object/inventory evidence and independent damaged-sign review remain outside this completed comparison. No Abydos object is joined to S9 by a shared personal name.
